title: Later — external module loading and activation planning
objective: Measure optional-module activation costs and turn the selected external-module use case into a validated implementation plan for a separately authored loader proof.
context_summary: Follows the core editor milestones and a documented selected external use case. Measures optional-module activation costs before planning a separately authored loader proof.

tasks.description: Measure optional-module activation and scope the required external-loader proof.
extra_context: Later extension work starts from the verified module-based editor and a documented chosen external use case. The four core milestones remain the next delivery sequence.
External binary loading is required even if measurements favor linked built-ins. This task scopes the loader proof; it does not deliver that loader.

context_links.label: Programmable operations and module host
context_links.relevance: Records accepted programmable-operation requirements, host/module responsibilities, staged delivery and measurable acceptance.

context_links.label: Module measurement protocol
context_links.relevance: Requires equivalent-output startup, memory, idle and first-use comparisons on the M4.

acceptance_criteria: Record the selected external module purpose/lifecycle and performance priorities in Markdown before designing a prototype; unresolved product tradeoffs stay explicit.
Compare cheap linked registration, lazy resources and relevant external loading on the verified editor with equivalent output; measure startup, memory, idle and first-use latency on native M4.
Define a separately authored loaded-module proof, including action/control discovery, host history, dependency/resource/trust boundaries, packaging, cancellation and missing-provider recovery.

Write a self-contained implementation plan with local IDs and verification for loading without host source changes, UI/API parity and preservation of existing edits; do not count an API client alone as module loading.

steps: Inspect the recorded use case and working editor contracts.
Measure equivalent-output configurations with the documented sampling protocol.
Review the proposed proof for real external loading and preserved source/history; validate its local DAG.
expected_results: Measurement-backed module boundaries and a scoped, executable plan for required external loading, with no fabricated speedup or implementation claim.
